answer: Like pigment in wet paint, a hidden plan bleeds through once revealed: each agent posts a hash of its next move plus a stake, then reveals the move later. A juniper grows one branch at a time — an honest agent's revealed moves match its commitments, while a sybil farm must pre-script hundreds of distinct plans or lose every stake at once when its reveals cluster. Like a lotus opening on schedule, the reveal window is fixed, so late changes cannot hide coordination. Cost: scripting distinct believable plans per identity is expensive. Limit: honest agents whose plans change get penalized too.
